abstracts.title: Influence from Arctic amplification on dissolved organic matter around Svalbard
abstracts.text: Svalbard is one of the most climate-sensitive regions of the rapidly warming Arctic, experiencing coastal glacier retreat and shifts in ocean circulation. Nearshore sea ice around Svalbard has substantially decreased in recent decades, driven by increased Atlantic Water (AW) inflow from the south combined with extended and warmer summers. These climatic and hydrographic changes alter biogeochemical cycling in coastal waters, leaving a diagnostic signature in the sources and composition of dissolved organic matter (DOM). Here, we investigated regional hydrographic influences on DOM characteristics by analyzing seawater samples collected in 2025 during a KOPRI-UiT Svalbard expedition at 30 stations across five regions, including western Spitsbergen (Transect 1), northern and southern Hinlopen (Transect 2), and eastern Nordaustlandet (Transect 3). The sampling included water-column stations along three Transects and surface-water stations outside the transect lines. Temperature-salinity characteristics confirmed distinct hydrographic regimes, with AW dominating Transect 1, mixed Arctic Water (ArW) and AW characterizing Transect 2, and cold and fresh ArW dominating Transect 3. These contrasting hydrographic conditions were accompanied by varied DOM concentrations (Transect 1; 1.4±0.3 mg/L, Transect 2; 1.3±0.7 mg/L, Transect 3; 1.0±0.1 mg/L) and their fractions including biopolymers (BP, pelagic algal and bacterial sources), humic substances (HS, terrestrial sources and microbial degradation), building blocks (BB, HS degradation), and low-molecular-weight compounds (LMW, sea-ice algal source and further degradation). The western region (Transect 1) was characterized by relatively high LMW (62%) and low HS (24%) contributions, whereas the eastern region (Transect 2 and 3) showed lower LMW (49%) and higher HS (34%) contributions. The predominance of LMW compounds in Transect 1 is consistent with a stronger contribution of marine algal DOM associated with warm, open Atlantic-influenced waters. Closer to coastal and fjord environments we note the presence of riverine and sea-ice algal DOM, leading to mixing of terrestrial and marine DOM sources. Transect 2 exhibited intermediate HS and relatively low LMW contributions, consistent with the presence of mixed ArW and AW. In contrast, Transect 3 showed a relatively high contribution of HS, consistent with a predominant contribution of terrestrially influenced and more processed DOM transported within Arctic-influenced waters. Overall, these spatial patterns suggest that DOM composition around Svalbard generate a distinct signatures for water-mass mixing (ArW and AW) and terrestrial inputs including glacier-derived DOM. Thus, our results suggest that DOM fingerprints reflect not only water-mass characteristics and sources but also the processing history of DOM during transport and mixing.

abstracts.title: Cyclic steps as a formative mechanism of morphodynamic and sedimentary heterogeneity in tidal-flat systems
abstracts.text: Tidal-flat successions are commonly characterized by heterolithic facies produced by alternating tidal currents, mud deposition, and periodic reworking. However, observations from modern macrotidal environments show that locally developed supercritical flows and cyclic steps can strongly modify these expected depositional patterns and generate pronounced morphodynamic and sediment heterogeneity. This study examines their occurrence and sedimentary significance using examples from the Sittaung River estuary, Myanmar, and the Yeochari tidal flat, Korea. In both settings, supercritical flows develop preferentially during the late stage of ebb tide, when drainage concentrates in shallow channels crossing relatively steep tidal-flat gradients. In the Sittunag estuary, blind tidal channels draining elevated inshore flats and tidal scour pools host breaking antidunes and cyclic steps ranging from meters to tens of meters. Progressive shallowing and channel confinement intensify supercritical conditions, producing repeated antidune growth, breaking, scour, and hydraulic jumps. These processes enhance downslope sediment transfer, maintain blind-channel morphology, and locally promote channel avulsion and rapid sediment redistribution. The resulting deposits are relatively coarse and well-sorted, with parallel to subparallel lamination, backset stratification, scour fills, and structureless to faintly laminated sands that sharply contrast with the surrounding muddy and heterolithic tidal-flat deposits. At Yeochari, supercritical late-ebb drainage produces a different but complementary expression of the same morphodynamic process. Cyclic steps and associated supercritical flows facilitate significant mud export from the tidal flat and induce rapid headward erosion of drainage channels. Repeated incision, retreat, and channel reorganization enhance lateral and vertical variability in point-bar deposits and contribute to the formation and preservation of muddy inclined heterolithic stratification. Thus, supercritical flows may both remove mud from actively scoured zones and indirectly promote muddy heterolithic accumulation through channel migration, abandonment, and bar construction. Together, these examples indicate that cyclic steps are not merely transient high-energy bedforms. They form part of a broader morphodynamic feedback between tidal-flat topography, drainage concentration, channel erosion, sediment bypass, and localized deposition. In Sittaung, this feedback produces coarse-grained sandy heterogeneity within otherwise muddy tidal-flat deposits, whereas in Yeochari it contributes to mud export, headward channel erosion, and the generation of muddy IHS. Cyclic steps and associated supercritical ebb flows may therefore represent an underrecognized formative mechanism for producing sedimentary heterogeneity in macrotidal-flat systems.

abstracts.title: Glacial impacts on sedimentation off Enderby land, east Antarctica during the past two glacial cycles
abstracts.text: The contribution from the land-based East Antarctic Ice Sheet to potential future sea level change remains uncertain, and its long-term behavior and sensitivity to climate forcing are poorly constrained. In this study, we present a high-resolution sedimentary record (core ANT37/C5-06) from the Cosmonaut Sea off Enderby Land, spanning the past two glacial cycles. End-member modelling of grain-size data reveals two primary sediment transport processes, including turbidity currents prevailing during glacials, and the Antarctic Slope Current (ASC) dominant during interglacials. Clay mineral assemblages indicate a predominant local sediment source, with smectite and kaolinite enriched during glacial periods reflecting enhanced erosion of proximal provenances, and illite representing background transport via the ASC or shelf dispersal. Our reconstructions reveal a more extensive ice sheet during Marine Isotope Stage (MIS) 6 than during the last glacial (MIS 4-2), and more substantial retreat during MIS 5 than the Holocene, with a progressive reduction through the MIS 5 interstadials. This pattern suggests accumulative melting in a synergistic response to both oceanic and atmospheric forcing. Circumpolar Deep Water driven melting acted as a continuous trigger, while snowfall accumulation associated with air temperature served as a critical buffer modulating ice mass balance. The results suggest a non-linear ice-sheet response to climate forcing. Our findings imply that prolonged, gradual ice melt from this sector could persist throughout the current interglacial, even if global warming is mitigated, and highlight the need to accurately represent these forcing mechanisms in ice sheet models.

abstracts.title: Impact of glacier meltwater runoff on flow patterns and seawater exchange processes in Kongsfjorden, Arctic Svalbard
abstracts.text: Glacier meltwater has been widely studied for its influence on hydrography within the inner fjord. However, its effects on shelf–fjord exchange at fjord mouths and circulation in the outer fjord remain less understood. This process is particularly important in western Svalbard, where warm Atlantic Water (AW) carried by the West Spitsbergen Current (WSC) can enter fjords through shelf–fjord exchange, thereby regulating oceanic heat transport to tidewater glaciers. This study aimed to quantify the effects of glacier meltwater runoff on shelf–fjord exchange and circulation in Kongsfjorden, Svalbard. To this end, high-resolution ocean modeling with a triangular unstructured grid was applied to Kongsfjorden by incorporating both surface and subsurface meltwater runoff. The model results show the glacier meltwater runoff strengthened density stratification and AW inflow at the fjord mouth. Glacier meltwater runoff controls shelf–fjord exchange by regulating estuarine circulation, thereby governing oceanic heat transport into inner fjords. This influx can significantly impact water temperature dynamics within the inner fjord, potentially accelerating glacier melting and affecting the local fjord ecosystem.

abstracts.title: The planform mobility of tidal channel confluences in the Dokgot-ri tidal flat, Garolim bay
abstracts.text: Fluvial confluences are generally characterized by limited mobility due to the development of well-defined scour holes. Previous studies have primarily focused on fluvial systems and microtidal environments, while quantitative investigations in macrotidal tidal flats remain limited. In addition, most studies have emphasized morphological characteristics, and morphodynamic approaches have been largely restricted to fluvial confluences. This study investigates the morphodynamic variability of tidal channels and their confluences in the macrotidal Dokgot-ri tidal flat in Garolim Bay. Seasonal drone-derived digital elevation models (DEMs) acquired between May 2023 and May 2025 were analyzed to quantify channel migration, sinuosity, asymmetry, confluence angle, and DEM of Difference. The results show that the confluence in the Dokgot-ri tidal flat exhibits active migration. Following channel piracy, the western upstream tributary developed increased sinuosity and gradually weakened, whereas a chute cut-off occurred in the eastern tributary. As a result, the confluence migrated with a clockwise rotation during the observation period. The confluence angle showed a continuous increase, while the associated scour hole remained poorly developed, to the extent that it was indistinguishable from the thalweg. The morphodynamic evolution of upstream tributaries played a key role in controlling confluence migration. Initially, the western tributary dominated the flow; however, as it weakened and the eastern tributary became progressively stronger, the confluence position shifted under the increasing influence of the eastern branch. Unlike fluvial confluences, no significant scour hole developed in the tidal channel confluence. This is likely because the tidal prism is substantially larger than the channel discharge, preventing the formation of sufficiently strong and persistent localized flows required to generate pronounced scour. The findings provide insights into tidal confluence dynamics in macrotidal environments and may serve as a basis for future comparative studies.

abstracts.title: Antarctic ice sheet areal expansion drove Middle Miocene Southern Ocean circulation shifts and CO2 drawdown
abstracts.text: The Early to Middle Miocene underwent dynamic climate reorganization driven by interactions between the ocean, atmosphere, and Antarctic Ice Sheet (AIS). Resolving how the Southern Ocean frontal and wind systems evolved, especially during the Middle Miocene Climate Transition [MMCT; 14.7–13.0 million years ago (Ma)], provides a crucial constraint on both the AIS growth and the role of oceanic CO2 drawdown. However, its evolutionary response remains completely elusive. Here, to reconstruct the evolution of these systems by tracing the associated Subantarctic Mode Water (SAMW), we investigated neodymium (Nd) isotope and foraminiferal geochemical records from Ocean Drilling Program Site 1120 (~550 m water depth) in the southwest Pacific. Our records capture an abrupt shift from a stratified, subtropical water-dominated state to active, wind-driven SAMW formation at ~14.2 Ma. This upper-ocean ventilation reorganization was likely driven by AIS expansion to coastal regions and the resultant intensification of wind systems. In addition, Nd isotope data reveal a shift at 13.5 Ma from nutrient-depleted initial SAMW to a modern-like, nutrient-rich Antarctic Surface Water-influenced SAMW. While SAMW formation persisted, this profound shift in its entrained water masses would have enhanced nutrient export from high to low latitudes, thereby stimulating regional primary productivity. We propose that areal expansion of the AIS drove the onset of SAMW formation; this evolving hydrographic feature and its changing water mass properties partly contributed to the combined efficiency of both physical and biological carbon pumps, thereby locking in the CO2-declining MMCT regime shift.

abstracts.title: Diagenetic overprint and magnetostratigraphic fidelity in central Arctic Ocean sediments
abstracts.text: The frequent geomagnetic reversals in central Arctic sediments have been widely questioned as faithful recording of changes in Earth’s magnetic field. Paleomagnetic and rock magnetic parameters from two gravity cores collected from the Alpha and Mendeleev ridges, western Arctic Ocean, have been analyzed to examine the preservation and alteration mechanisms of magnetostratigraphic signals. Paleomagnetic results indicate that the remanence records in the upper sections of the cores are poorly preserved, whereas the lower part contains a recognizable inclination reversal section that allow for regional correlation. Rock magnetic analyses reveal significant diagenesis, with distinct differences in composition of magnetic minerals between the upper and lower part of the cores. Age constraints established based on biostratigraphy and manganese cycles suggest that the variations in magnetic minerals appear to correlate more strongly with core depth than with age. The primary remanent magnetization in the upper parts of the cores is likely obscured by a strong, inseparable chemical remanent magnetization (CRM) resulting from intense diagenesis. Variations in the redox environment of Arctic Ocean Bottom Water could be a crucial factor contributing to the CRM changes in magnetic minerals within sediments, ultimately leading to anomalous magnetic inclination signals.

abstracts.title: Multi-indicator identification of sediment-source responses and hydrodynamic reworking in typhoon event deposits: A case study from the northeastern Beibu Gulf
abstracts.text:
Typhoons are episodic forcing events that rapidly alter terrigenous input, seabed resuspension, particle transport, and sediment preservation in low-latitude shelf seas and semi-enclosed bays. Their event deposits record extreme land–sea material transport and serve as modern analogues for paleo-typhoon interpretation.

This study examines northeastern Beibu Gulf after Super Typhoon Yagi (2024). Surface muddy event layers and underlying sediments were analyzed for grain-size, organic carbon, and lipid biomarkers, rare earth elements (REEs), and heavy metals to characterize provenance, transport, and geochemical signatures. A laterally continuous yellowish-brown fluid-mud layer (0.5–1.0 cm thick) was widely observed, distinct in color, structure, and grain-size, with finer particles, elevated TOC/TN, and enriched biomarkers. It is identified as a fine-grained typhoon deposit formed mainly during the post-storm recovery stage.

Lipid biomarkers show concurrent enrichment of terrestrial and marine phytoplankton markers, indicating enhanced terrigenous input, productivity response, and organic preservation. A biomarker-based transport index suggests near-source rapid deposition in the central nearshore and stronger distal signals along eastern/western sectors. REE patterns retain a regional mixed-source background, but decoupling between LREEs and HREEs implies non-equilibrium geochemical reorganization under short-term disturbance. Heavy metals are generally enriched in the event layer, but Al-normalized interlayer differences weaken, suggesting that apparent enrichment is mainly controlled by fine-grained, Al-rich aluminosilicates and organic matter, not by enhanced external pollution.

Overall, the event layer represents a composite unit formed by enhanced terrestrial supply, resuspension, distal fine-particle transport, productivity response, carrier-phase reorganization, and post-storm settling. Provenance changes reflect event-scale remixing and reweighting of existing sediment sources and pools, rather than new source replacement. Our multi-proxy framework provides a useful reference for identifying modern typhoon event deposits, interpreting paleo-records, and evaluating post-typhoon environmental effects in muddy semi-enclosed bays and shelves.

abstracts.title: Productivity regulated by overturning circulation in the Southern Ocean since the late Pliocene
abstracts.text: The Southern Ocean plays a key role in regulating the global carbon cycle through biological pump and ocean circulation, which likely drove critical global climatic transitions during the late Cenozoic. In this study, using a sediment core from the Cooperation Sea, East Antarctica, we integrated analyses of biogenic opal content, foraminiferal abundance, and XRF scanning data to reconstruct the history of productivity and circulation in this region since the late Pliocene, spanning ~3 million years. Our data show a decline in siliceous productivity at 1.6 Ma, likely due to climate cooling and enhanced stratification, followed by persistently low values during the middle Pleistocene. Siliceous productivity then increased substantially and fluctuated drastically after the Mid-Brunhes Event (~430ka), attributed to warmer climate and stronger upwelling during interglacials. Variations in siliceous productivity reflect the migration of the Southern Ocean frontal system. Calcareous productivity proxies remained extremely low before the middle Pleistocene and then increased markedly during the middle Pleistocene. Notably, they exhibit higher values during glacials than interglacials in the late Pleistocene. These changes are attributed to changes in carbonate preservation, modulated by the intensity of Antarctic Bottom Water formation, which affects bottom-water carbonate corrosivity.

abstracts.title: Enhanced Arctic sea-ice retreat due to pronounced pacificization effect in the Holocene
abstracts.text: Future climate confronts major challenges due to ongoing Arctic sea-ice retreat. Notably, eventful sea ice loss in the Holocene appears comparable circumstance, but associated physics remians poorly understood. Here we present a high-resolution and semi-quantitative reconstruction of sea-ice conditions over the East Siberian Arctic Shelf. A compilation of sea-ice reconstructions across the circum-Arctic characterizes a Pacific-side Arctic sea-ice melting (‘PASIM’) event between 4.5 and 2.2 ka BP (Figure 1A). Together with basin-wide paleoclimate records, satellite-derived and numerical modeling datasets, we attribute this sea-ice melting event to enhanced Bering Sea Inflow with stronger poleward transport of Pacific oceanic heat (Figure 1B-C), which overcame long-term Holocene cooling trend likely linked to concurrently slowing Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation. Such Holocene-scale competition effect of ‘Pacificization v.s. Atlantification’ may conceptually explain the modern dipole pattern in Arctic sea-ice variation. In the warming future, projected more frequent La Niña circumstance could indicate enhanced Pacificization effect, leading to aggravated Pacific-side Arctic sea-ice retreat.

abstracts.title: Geomorphological control on hydrodynamics and sediment transport in a hypertidal, human-altered bay: Gyeonggi Bay, Korea
abstracts.text: The west coast of Korea shows a large tidal range and high concentration of suspended sediments. A complicated coastline and anthropogenic alterations have affected local hydrodynamics and sediment transport. However, the hydrodynamics and sediment resuspension characteristics still remain poorly understood owing to the complicated tidal characteristics. Also, several tidal sandbars near the coastline compartmentalized the channel network, creating distinct sedimentary environments. In this study, comprehensive field observations were conducted at Gyeonggi Bay, which has undergone major alterations, to elucidate the hydrodynamic and benthic sedimentary differences between the main channel (transect AA' and station M1) and the channel enclosed by tidal sandbars (transect BB' and station M2). The cross-sectional hydrodynamic environments (current velocity and sediment resuspension) and suspended particle characteristics were measured through ship-borne surveys during tidal cycles. Time series of hydrodynamic characteristics were measured by mooring systems. In the main channel, current velocities through the water column and benthic turbulence at 25 cm above the bed were measured. In the enclosed channel, benthic turbulence at two heights (25 cm and 140 cm above the bed) was measured (Figure 1). The main channel showed an ebb-dominant hydrodynamic environment with higher current velocities and sediment resuspension during both the spring and neap tides. The benthic shear stress repeatedly increased during ebb tides. The suspended sediment fractal dimension and settling velocity slightly increased from high to low tides, indicating the formation of larger sediment flocs. Meanwhile, the enclosed channel showed comparable current velocity and sediment resuspension between flood and ebb tides during both the spring and neap tides. The benthic shear stress fluctuation showed an opposite trend compared to the main channel, with repeated increases during flood tides likely due to the flow constriction through the narrow channel. The suspended sediment fractal dimension and settling velocity also showed no difference between high and low tides. The results imply that the main channel has been affected by different sediment inputs from the flood (sourced from the Yellow Sea) and ebb (sourced from the Han River), resulting in active exchange of suspended sediment with adjacent waters. However, the tidal sandbars around the enclosed channel limited the exchange of suspended sediment, resulting in similar hydrodynamic and sedimentary characteristics. These results suggest that tidal sandbar-driven separation can create markedly different hydrodynamic regimes over distances of only a few kilometers, highlighting the sensitivity of tidal channel systems to geomorphological change in human-altered bays.

abstracts.title: Changing Modes of Biogenic Sedimentation in the Ross Sea Sector Across the Mid-Pleistocene Transition
abstracts.text: The Mid-Pleistocene Transition (MPT), which occurred roughly one million years ago, was a major change in Earth’s climate system, marked by global cooling, increasing ice volume, and a shift in glacial-interglacial cycles from about 41,000 to 100,000 years. Although the Southern Ocean may have played an important role in this transition, records spanning the MPT remain limited, particularly in the Ross Sea sector. To better understand environmental changes in this region, we analyzed two sediment cores collected from the Ross Sea continental rise, focusing on biogenic opal, calcium carbonate (CaCO3), nitrogen isotopes, and sediment grain size. Before the MPT, the region was characterized by high diatom productivity and nutrient-rich surface waters, with little or no CaCO3 preserved in the sediments. During the MPT, diatom production declined and the upper ocean became more strongly stratified, creating conditions that likely favored greater CaCO3 preservation, as supported by increasing nitrogen isotope values and higher coccolith abundances. After the MPT, stratification became even stronger, while carbonate preservation continued to improve and eventually extended into deeper waters during the late Pleistocene. These results suggest that the MPT was associated with a major reorganization of the marine environment in the Ross Sea sector, shifting the dominant type of biogenic sediment from silica-rich diatom material to carbonate-rich deposits.

abstracts.title: Linking molecular fingerprints with isotopic and biomarker evidence to resolve sedimentary organic matter sources in the Arctic
abstracts.text: Accurately identifying and quantifying the sources of sedimentary organic matter (OM) is key to elucidating the transport and fate of terrestrial carbon mobilized under ongoing Arctic warming (Martens et al., 2022). Carbon isotopes, particularly δ13C and Δ14C, are widely used to distinguish marine and terrestrial carbon sources and constrain their ages in Arctic marine sediments, but their source specificity can be limited by overlapping signatures among different carbon pools (Lamb et al., 2006). Lipid biomarkers offer greater source specificity but represent only a small fraction of the molecular diversity of organic-solvent-extractable OM (Zhang et al., 2026). Recent advances in ultrahigh resolution mass spectrometry, such as Fourier transform ion cyclotron resonance mass spectrometry (FT-ICR MS), enable the detection and assignment of thousands of molecular formulas within a single sample, providing a detailed molecular perspective on complex OM (Menges et al., 2022). Here, we developed an integrated framework combining carbon isotopes, lipid biomarkers, and molecular fingerprints to investigate the sources and molecular composition of sedimentary OM along the Yenisei-Kara Sea transect. Based on contrasting geographic and environmental conditions, the transect was divided into three distinct zones, for which a dual-isotope mixing model was used to quantify the contributions of marine, riverine, and erosion derived organic carbon (OC). By correlating molecular formulas with isotopic and biomarker evidence, we identified three diagnostic molecular groups (mA-Peaks, rA-Peaks, and eA-Peaks) associated with marine, riverine, and erosion derived OM, respectively. Their different elemental compositions and molecular characteristics were subsequently used to develop a molecular-parameter mixing model for source apportionment. Source contribution estimates from the dual-isotope and molecular-parameter models showed a significant positive correlation and broadly consistent spatial patterns across the three zones. These findings highlight the potential of FT-ICR MS-derived molecular information to complement isotopic and biomarker approaches, providing a more comprehensive understanding of sedimentary OM sources in Arctic environments.

abstracts.title: Tidal controls on suspended sediment from space
abstracts.text:
Satellite observations are not only limited by missing data; they can also contain deterministic physical biases. Correcting such biases is therefore essential for revealing the tidal processes embedded in satellite-derived suspended sediment concentration (SSC). Here, we develop a physics-guided framework that integrates analytical sediment transport theory with high-frequency satellite observations (GOCI) to investigate tidal controls on coastal SSC dynamics in Korea Bay.

We first demonstrate that fixed daylight sampling can become phase-locked with solar tidal variability, introducing a systematic “daylight bias” into long-term SSC estimates. This bias occurs because periodic SSC variations driven by solar tides can be aliased into the climatological mean when satellite observations repeatedly capture specific tidal phases. A harmonic fitting approach is developed to separate the background SSC state from solar-tide-induced variations, thereby reducing systematic errors caused by satellite sampling limitations.

Building on this correction framework, we further resolve SSC responses induced by M2 and S2 tidal forcing and their nonlinear sediment-resuspension signatures. A theory-guided harmonic decomposition successfully extracts SSC responses associated with M2/S2 tidal forcing and their nonlinear resuspension-generated components (M4, MS4, and MSf) despite nonuniform sampling. The retrieved harmonic signals show quantitative agreement with analytical model predictions, enabling the separation of sediment transport mechanisms dominated by horizontal advection and local resuspension. Based on these physically resolved tidal signatures, a tidal resuspension index is developed to identify spatial transitions among advection-dominated, transitional, and resuspension-dominated sediment transport regimes across Korea Bay.

This study demonstrates that satellite sampling limitations and tidal sediment dynamics are physically coupled rather than independent challenges. By combining deterministic bias correction with mechanism-based harmonic analysis, satellite remote sensing can be transformed from descriptive observation into quantitative diagnosis of coastal sediment transport processes. The proposed framework provides a transferable approach for investigating tidally controlled sediment dynamics and other periodically varying coastal environmental variables from space.

abstracts.title: Long-term paleoceanographic change in the north Crozet region (Indian sector of the Southern Ocean) during the last ~3 Ma
abstracts.text: The Antarctic Circumpolar Current (ACC) plays a key role in transporting heat, carbon, and nutrients in the Southern Ocean. Its associated oceanic fronts separate water masses with distinct physical and biogeochemical properties and regulate nutrient availability and surface productivity in each frontal zone. The North Crozet region, located in the Indian sector of the Southern Ocean, lies in the pathway of the ACC, and the Subantarctic Front (SAF) near the Crozet Islands is strongly constrained by regional bathymetry. However, the long-term records of paleoceanographic changes associated with variability in the ACC frontal system remain poorly constrained in the Crozet region. MD218 CROTALE expedition aimed to recover the long sedimentary records in the Crozet region to investigate the temporal and spatial variability of the ACC, together with changes in paleoproductivity and associated biogeochemical changes, focussing on the long-term paleoceanographic changes. The 69.7 m long core (MD19-3581) was collected from the North Crozet at a water depth of 2,295 m. Here we document the geochemical properties (CaCO3, biogenic opal, total organic carbon, total nitrogen), sediment organic carbon isotope (δ13C), and grain size of detrital particles with end-member modelling analysis. The age model established using planktonic foraminiferal oxygen isotope (δ¹⁸O) stratigraphy indicates that core MD19-3581 spans approximately 3.2 Ma. The geochemical records show both glacial–interglacial variability following the general trend in Subantarctic Zone and the long-term pronounced changes. A three-end-member solution was obtained, with modal grain sizes of 6.7 μm (EM1), 86 μm (EM2), and 272 μm (EM3). In the presentation, we will discuss further the long-term paleoceanographic changes (e.g., iNHG, MPT) in terms of paleoproductivity as well as the sediment transport responded to the front migrations associated with ACC strength variability.

abstracts.title: Enhanced organic-carbon burial under reduced deep-water oxygenation in the western Arctic during the late Middle Pleistocene Transition
abstracts.text:
The Mid-Pleistocene Transition (MPT, ~1.2-0.7 Ma) marks a fundamental reorganization of the global climate system, in which changes in Arctic Ocean environment have been inferred as a key driver through modulating the carbon reservoir by ice sheet dynamics and ocean circulation processes. In this study, we use geochemical redox proxies, Fe and Mo isotopes, and productivity indicators from sediment core ARC7-LIC (Canada Basin, ~1.9 Ma) to reconstruct the oxygenation state and carbon storage of the Arctic Ocean’s sedimentary environment across the MPT, with provenance indicators constraining potential source effects on the isotope records.

Provenance indicators suggest primarily sediment input from the Siberian Arctic, with increasing contributions from the Laurentide discharge towards the late Pleistocene. The Fe and Mo isotope records suggest a progressive decline in bottom-water oxygenation prior to the MPT (1.9-1.2 Ma). While during the early MPT (1.2– 1.0 Ma), shifts in isotope compositions indicate an improvement in bottom-water oxygenation, coincident with the opening of the Barents seaway, which facilitated enhanced inflow of North Atlantic water that briefly re-ventilated the deep basin. In the late MPT (1.0–0.7 Ma), the isotopes record a deterioration of oxygenation conditions, possibly related to ice sheet and perennial sea-ice expansion.

This late-MPT TOC burial peak coincided with the global atmospheric CO2 minimum and large-scale Northern Hemisphere ice-sheet expansion. We propose that the Arctic Ocean augmented the deep-sea carbon reservoir through redox-driven carbon sequestration, while its freshwater export may have further suppressed NADW formation and weakened AMOC, amplifying global carbon storage. Together, these processes established a positive feedback loop by more carbon burial, lower atmospheric CO2, and further ice-sheet growth, which helped stabilize the 100-kyr glacial-interglacial cycle. Our findings integrate the Arctic Ocean into the global carbon cycle framework of the MPT and demonstrate that high-latitude basins, through their sensitivity to ice cover and freshwater forcing, can exert a critical influence on global climate transitions via feedbacks among ocean ventilation, redox chemistry, and carbon burial.

abstracts.title: Variability of cohesive sediment erodibility across diverse depositional environments
abstracts.text: Cohesive sediment erodibility varies substantially with sediment properties and environmental conditions. Although various experimental devices and erosion parameters have been used to quantify erodibility, differences in measurement approaches and parameterization make direct comparison among previous studies difficult. Erodibility is commonly represented by the initial critical shear stress for erosion (tc0) or erosion rate (E). However, tc0 represents only the onset of erosion, while E varies with the magnitude and duration of applied bed shear stress. Therefore, neither parameter alone necessarily represents the overall susceptibility of a sediment bed to erosion. In this study, the erosion rate coefficient (M), which represents the erosion response to applied shear stress, was used as a practical metric of cohesive sediment erodibility. Erosion experiments conducted using the Gust Erosion Microcosm System (GEMS) were compiled across diverse depositional environments, including tidal flats, tidal channels, salt marshes, bays, harbours, and the deep sea. Both M and the friction coefficient (f) were derived from the GEMS experiments. f, which has been widely used in Sea Carousel studies to characterize changes in bed erosion resistance, was compared with M to examine whether the two parameters could provide an empirical basis for integrating erosion datasets obtained using different approaches. An overall inverse relationship was observed between M and f, with higher M generally associated with lower f. Their distributions also differed among depositional environments. Bay sediments were characterized by relatively high M and low f, whereas salt-marsh and some tidal-channel sediments were concentrated in the low M, high f range. Tidal-flat sediments exhibited a broader range of erodibility. These results suggest that M and f, although representing different aspects of the erosion process, may provide complementary measures of cohesive sediment erodibility. Their empirical relationship offers a potential framework for integrating erosion datasets obtained using different measurement approaches and for investigating environmental controls on cohesive sediment erodibility.

abstracts.title: Grain size change of detrital particles in the Antarctic zone (Conrad Rise) of the Southern Ocean since the last glacial maximum
abstracts.text: A 10.47 m long piston core (COR-1bPC) was collected at the Conrad Rise located south of the Antarctic Polar Front (i.e., Antarctic Zone) in the Indian sector of the Southern Ocean. High-resolution multi-proxy paleoceanographic data exhibit the distinct temporal variation of surface water paleoproductivity from the last glacial through deglacial to Holocene. Biogenic opal and CaCO3 contents increased gradually and intermittently, respectively, from the last glacial period to the Holocene. Such paleoproductivity increase in the Antarctic Zone has been attributable to the reduced sea ice coverage and more nutrient supply by resumed upwelling of Circumpolar Deep Water. In this study, a total of 87 samples of core COR-1bPC were selected for the grain size analysis of detrital fraction, after removing the organic matter, CaCO3, and biogenic silica. Grain size end member (EM) modelling was conducted using AnalySize with nonparametric analysis. In addition, the mean sortable silt (SS mean), a proxy for relative bottom current strength, was calculated. Five EMs are extracted from the grain size distributions of all analyzed samples, which are EM1 (11.5 μm), EM2 (25.1 μm), EM3 (32.5 μm), EM4 (45.9 μm), and EM5 (84.3 μm). EM1 consists of the very fine-grained sediments, representing the aeolian particles. EM2, EM3, and EM4 belong to the silt-sized particles. EM5 is very coarse-grained particles including ice-rafted debris. Individual EM contributions are different from the last glacial period to the Holocene. In particular, contribution of EM1 is intensified during the Holocene, playing an important role to deliver aeolian Fe-bearing particles in enhancing the surface water productivity. Finally, based on SS mean, the bottom current speed was intensified during the deglacial period, but the SS mean was not efficient during the last glacial period because of poor relationship between the SS mean and abundance of sortable silt.

abstracts.title: Wildfire history recorded in deposits of the East Siberian Arctic Shelf since the late Quaternary
abstracts.text: Wildfires and black carbon are key to understanding the global carbon cycle and climate change, especially in the rapidly warming Arctic. In this study, we analyze black carbon and stable carbon isotope of sedimentary core LV 90-8-1 on the East Siberian Arctic shelf to trace Arctic wildfire history since the last interglacial period. Our findings indicate that extreme warm/humid conditions during MIS 5e-c and MIS 1, as well as extreme cold/dry periods in MIS 4 and MIS 2, suppressed wildfire occurrence due to reduced fuel dryness and limited combustibles, respectively. In contrast, during the milder climatic conditions of MIS 5b and MIS 3, wildfires increased during warm stages and decreased during cold stages, correlating with Dansgaard-Oeschger cycles, largely driven by variations in fuel availability. The study underscores that frequent wildfires driven by climate may further intensify the Arctic warming through positive feedbacks.

abstracts.title: Long-term evolution of tidal channel networks in an accretional tidal flat in a macrotidal setting
abstracts.text:
Tidal channel networks dissecting intertidal flats are common landforms that generate spatial heterogeneity in tidal-flat stratigraphy and evolve in response to changes in sediment supply derived from hydrodynamic regimes. Their morphometric characteristics can therefore provide insights into the long-term geomorphic evolution of coastal depositional systems. This study investigates the decadal-scale evolution of tidal channel networks on the Donggeom tidal flat, Gyeonggi Bay, west coast of Korea, using aerial photographs and satellite imagery spanning 57 years (1966–2023). Thirteen channel networks were extracted from images acquired in 1966, 1992, 2003, 2014, and 2023. Changes in total channel length, main-channel length, junction number, network area, and annualized relative change rate were quantified.

The Donggeom tidal flat substantially expanded between 1966 and 2003 as a former north–south-oriented branch of the Yeomha Channel progressively infilled. This accretion followed the upstream closure of the channel associated with coastal development, which reduced fluvial influence and likely altered tidal asymmetry and sediment transport toward depositional conditions. Channel network development varied spatially across the tidal flat. Networks on pre-existing tidal flats showed relatively limited changes in network extent and branching complexity, whereas substantial expansion and branching occurred along the former subtidal-channel corridor. Initially simple or poorly developed networks within this corridor progressively increased in channel length and junction number as the subtidal channel was converted into an intertidal flat.

Channel network development also exhibited a distinct temporal progression. Upstream networks developed earlier and subsequently showed lower rates of morphological change, whereas downstream networks continued to expand and branch through 2023. This spatiotemporal pattern suggests a downstream progression of channel-network initiation, expansion, and stabilization associated with progressive infilling of the former subtidal channel. The preferential development of networks along this corridor further indicates that antecedent morphology exerted a persistent control on subsequent channel organization, reflecting geomorphic memory during tidal-flat development. These results demonstrate that the evolution from a subtidal channel to an accretional tidal flat involves not only sediment accumulation but also systematic reorganization of the channel network, with the location and timing of network development conditioned by antecedent morphology. Given the role of the Yeomha Channel as one of the major pathways for river-derived sediments to the extensive tidal flats of inner Gyeonggi Bay, the observed channel-network evolution provides a geomorphic record of long-term sediment redistribution and offers insights into the response of the depositional system to changing sediment pathways.

abstracts.title: Reconstructing lower circumpolar deep-water variations during glacial–interglacial periods with ferromanganese-coated IRDs from the Drake Passage
abstracts.text: The Drake Passage, a critical pathway of the Antarctic Circumpolar Current (ACC), links the Atlantic, Pacific, and Indian Oceans and serves as a major gateway for Circumpolar Deep Water (CDW). Deep-water circulation here has shifted over glacial–interglacial cycles, influencing oxygen-rich deep-water inflow and associated bottom-water oxidation, with important implications for the marine environment. This study examines ferromanganese-coated ice-rafted debris (Fe–Mn-coated IRD) from the 591 cm sediment core GC06-DP04, spanning approximately 2.25 Ma, collected in the Drake Passage (58°56.9212′S, 62°39.3129′W; 3,851 m water depth) during the 2005 R/V Yuzhmorgeologiya expedition conducted by the Korea Polar Research Institute (KOPRI). IRD samples obtained from 13 depths were analyzed using micro-computed tomography (μ-CT), micro-X-ray fluorescence (μ-XRF), and Raman spectroscopy. The coatings were generally thin but reached a maximum thickness of ~980 μm, and vernadite was identified in all samples. The average Mn/Fe ratio was 0.54, consistent with a hydrogenetic origin and formation under oxic seawater conditions. Intervals characterized by thicker coatings and lower Mn/Fe ratios coincided with decreases in mean grain size and sand + gravel content, together with increases in Fe₂O₃ and MnO concentrations. These changes indicate enhanced oxic conditions during interglacial periods, and the lower Mn/Fe ratios may also reflect an increased supply of dissolved Fe through deep-water circulation. Furthermore, these patterns suggest that a strengthened Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) enhanced the southward transport of North Atlantic Deep Water (NADW), which contributes to the formation of Lower Circumpolar Deep Water (LCDW), a major pathway for dissolved Fe transport into the Southern Ocean. Increased inflow of oxygen-rich LCDW into the Drake Passage may therefore have enhanced both Fe supply and seafloor oxygenation, promoting Fe–Mn oxide precipitation on IRD surfaces. Therefore, the mineralogical and geochemical characteristics of Fe–Mn-coated IRD provide information distinct from conventional sediment-based proxies and may serve as a novel proxy for reconstructing changes in deep-water circulation and paleoclimate variability in the Drake Passage.

abstracts.title: Glacial loading and unloading influence fault stresses and fluid migration beneath the western bathymetry trough
abstracts.text: Evidence suggesting repeated advances and retreats of marine-based ice sheets during Quaternary glaciations has been identified in the Western Bathymetric Trough (WBT) along the western margin of the Chukchi Rise. However, the relationship between glacially induced fault stress changes and subsurface fluid migration remains poorly constrained. We combined multichannel seismic reflection (MCS) data with numerical modeling to examine fault stress evolution and potential fluid migration pathways beneath the WBT. Interpretation of the MCS data identified 14 normal faults with bright spots concentrated near the upper fault tips and fault zones. A two-way coupled Elmer/Ice–PyLith model simulated ice sheet evolution and viscoelastic crust–mantle deformation from 191 to 0 ka BP. The timing of prescribed glaciation–deglaciation forcing was constrained by the global benthic oxygen isotope stack. Modeled grounding line advances developed during Marine Isotope Stages (MIS) 6, 5d, 5b, and 4. In the simulations, major advances during MIS 6 and 4 produced subsidence beneath the ice load, followed by uplift during deglaciation. Normal and shear stress changes were evaluated for the seaward (F01-F11) and landward (F12-F14) fault groups relative to the stress state at 191 ka BP. Reduced normal compression favored an opening tendency in the seaward fault group over most of the simulation period. The landward fault group alternated between opening and clamping tendencies, with a stronger clamping tendency. Vertically stacked bright spots were observed across sedimentary layers near the upper tips and fault zones of the seaward faults. The spatial association between bright spots and faults exhibiting a modeled opening tendency suggests a possible link between stress redistribution during glacial loading and unloading and upward fluid migration along pre-existing faults.

abstracts.title: Compilation of the 1:1,000,000 sediment type map of China’s adjacent seas: Data integration, classification standards and mapping practice
abstracts.text: Sediment type maps of China's adjacent seas serve as a fundamental basis for understanding sediment composition, provenance, transport, deposition, and paleoenvironmental evolution in this region. They also provide essential baseline data and scientific support for marine engineering construction, fisheries, mineral resource exploration, marine ecological conservation, and navigation safety. In recent years, based on more than 26,000 stations, we have compiled and published the Sediment Type Map of the Bohai, Yellow and East China Seas and the Sediment Type Map of the South China Sea. The maps identify 62 sediment types, and also delineate the distribution of hard substrates including rocks, polymetallic nodules, coral reefs, and crusts. The maps and accompanying explanatory notes elucidate the types, distribution patterns, variation trends, and sediment budgets of surface sediments in China's marginal seas, and further discuss the controlling factors and underlying mechanisms. Future work will focus on multi-source data fusion and standardization processing, promote the unification of sediment classification standards, and explore new generation digital mapping technologies to continuously improve the accuracy and application value of maps.

abstracts.title: Cycladophora davisiana (Radiolaria) curve in the Bering and Okhotsk Seas since the Last Glacial Maximum considering sieve sizes and morphology

Micropaleontologists have used different-sized meshes (45 µm and 63 µm) to estimate the C. davisiana abundance. However, no study has evaluated how sieve mesh sizes change the C. davisiana abundance and test size by processing specific samples sieving with 45 µm and 63 µm meshes. We performed microscopic observation to investigate changes in C. davisiana abundance and test size in the Bering and Okhotsk Seas since the last glacial maximum (LGM) using different-sized meshes (45 µm and 63 µm). Two sediment core samples were used: BOW-9A from the Bowers Ridge in the Bering Sea and XP98-PC2 from the central Okhotsk Sea. In the Bering Sea, the relative abundance of C. davisiana in both size fractions (45-63 µm and >63 µm) increased toward the last glacial period. The absolute abundances (No. tests g-1) of both >63 µm and 45-63 µm fractions showed peaks at ~14 ka and ~3 ka, respectively. In the Okhotsk Sea, the relative abundances were high (>40%) in the 45-63 µm fraction, whereas low (<20%) in the >63 µm fraction during the last deglacial-glacial period. An absolute abundance peak was found in the 45-63 µm fraction during the middle Holocene, but not for the >63 µm fraction. The morphometric analysis to measure the 3rd and 4th segment widths of C. davisiana showed that their size maximized at ~14 ka in the Bering Sea and gradually increased from the last glacial period to the present in the Okhotsk Sea. Based on the lines of evidence, we discuss changes in intermediate-water ventilation across the Bering Sea and Okhotsk Seas over the past 25 ka.

abstracts.title: Evolution history of a submarine mud volcano in the inner-shelf off southeastern Korea
abstracts.text: This study investigates the morphology and evolution of a mud volcano in the inner shelf off southeastern Korea. We integrated Chirp seismic profiles, multi-beam bathymetry, and sediment core analyses to identify its structural development until present. The mound structure exhibits an elliptical shape oriented NE-SW with a height of 20 m. Cone-shaped small mounds are identified in the mound structure and are interpreted as cold-water coral (CWC) mounds. CWC mounds are distributed on the crest and northeastern flank of the mound, whereas lobe structures, interpreted as sediment flow, are distributed along the southwestern and southern flank. Sediment cores filled with mud and coral fragments revealed that CWCs colonized at the mound after the formation of the mound. The identified mound structure is interpreted as a mud volcano evidenced by the size, common features (diapir, lobe). According to the radiocarbon age, the mud volcano formed earlier than 7.1 ka BP. After the development of the mud volcano, corals colonized its crest. The Tsushima Current transported fine-grained sediments, leading to coral mortality. At present, the bottom currents corresponding to the Tsushima Current erode the northeastern flank and surrounding area, forming the steep slope and depressions.

abstracts.title: Multiphase glaciation in East Siberia during the late Quaternary: Evidence from Arctic zircon U-Pb ages
abstracts.text: Tracing ice-rafted debris (IRD) in Arctic Ocean sediments is critical for understanding the evolution of Northern Hemisphere ice cover. However, differentiating sediment sources from the circum-Arctic continental shelves has long posed a challenge in identifying IRD origins. In this study, we present a comprehensive provenance analysis based on 7570 detrital zircon U-Pb ages, encompassing surface sediments from circum-Arctic continental shelves and IRD from deep-sea cores in the central Arctic Ocean. Our results reveal distinctive zircon age distributions corresponding to different regions of the circum-Arctic shelves. Notably, sediments from the East Siberian continental shelf are uniquely characterized by a dual peak in zircon ages at ~90–100 Ma and ~150 Ma. Similar zircon age distributions are identified in IRD from the central Arctic Ocean, appearing during at least four glacial periods. This provides evidence that iceberg-carried debris from the East Siberian continental shelf was transported to the central Arctic, indicating the presence of an ice sheet or glaciers on the East Siberian shelf during multiple glacial periods. This study underscores the importance of integrating sediment provenance analysis with ice-sheet dynamics to refine our understanding of Arctic climate evolution.

abstracts.title: Orbital forcing on coccolithophore assemblages in the Solomon Sea during the last 260 ka
abstracts.text: The Solomon Sea is a locus of intermixing of various water masses contributing not only to waters of the West Pacific Warm Pool, but also to the Equatorial Undercurrent (EUC) that eventually upwells at the East Pacific. Therefore, the Solomon Sea is an integral location for investigating high–low latitude climatic and oceanographic teleconnections. Despite this importance, ecological proxies from the Solomon Sea remain scarce. Here, we analyze coccolithophore assemblages from the Solomon Sea during the last 260 ka from ODP Site 1115B, documenting paleoceanographic changes in the area during the last three glacial terminations in conjunction with previously published physicochemical records from the areaa. We found strong glacial–interglacial variability in our coccolithophore assemblage composition and coccolithophore-derived net primary productivity (NPP). Interglacial stages generally correspond to an increase in the proportion of the lower photic zone species Florisphaera indicate obliquity- and precession-like cyclicities, but only the obliquity signal shows a consistent relationship with kyr study interval. The exact mechanisms are still currently under investigation, but we hypothesize that the obliquity signal may be related to equator–pole insolation changes that impact the advection of South Pacific Tropical Water to the Solomon Seaa,b. However, this variability might also arise from obliquity-driven interhemispheric interactions between the Siberian High and Australian Low which changes the strength of cross-equatorial northerly winds and the position of the Intertropical Convergence Zonec and, therefore, SST, TT, nutrient, and NPP changes in the Solomon Sea. Our work underscores the underappreciated role of obliquity-driven variations in coccolithophore assemblages and NPP in the tropics, which might have important implications on the nutrient content of waters that upwells at the East Pacific via the EUC.

abstracts.title: Quantitative integration of geostatistics and rock physics analysis for uncertainty evaluation in “Giddy” Field, offshore Niger Delta
abstracts.text: Reservoir characterization in the structurally complex offshore Niger Delta is challenged by lithological heterogeneity, fault compartmentalization, and sparse well control. This study presents a quantitative framework that integrates geostatistics and rock physics to reduce spatial and lithological uncertainties and to derive probabilistic hydrocarbon volumes for the “Giddy” Field. Four wells (J1–J4) with gamma ray, resistivity, density, neutron, and sonic logs, plus check-shot data, were integrated with a 3D seismic volume (274 inlines, 256 crosslines). Seismic interpretation (ant-tracking, variance edge) mapped NE-SW trending normal faults and delineated three reservoirs (R1–R3) within the Agbada Formation. Petrophysical properties—shale volume (Stieber), porosity, water saturation (Archie), and permeability (Timur)—were computed and upscaled onto a 3D structural grid. Spatial continuity was modeled via variograms and Sequential Gaussian Simulation (SGS). Rock physics analysis used P-impedance, Vp/Vs, and λρ–μρ cross-plots for lithology/fluid discrimination. Monte Carlo Simulation (20 realizations) quantified uncertainty in net rock volume and Stock Tank Oil Initially In Place (STOIIP). Vsh ranges from 0.012 to 0.45, while porosity varies between 0.003 and 0.32 across wells. Rock physics cross-plots reveal clean sandstones clustering at low γ-ray values, low λρ, and moderate μρ, diagnostic of high-porosity, hydrocarbon-bearing intervals. Seismic inversion and attribute analysis confirm fault-bounded anticlinal traps with strong amplitude anomalies aligned to reservoir tops. SGS realizations capture pronounced lateral heterogeneity, with porosity variance of 16–24% and permeability ranging 150–400 mD due to uncalibrated log-derived transforms. Water saturation ranges 25–35%, influenced by capillary pressure assumptions. Probabilistic volumetric outcomes are: net reservoir volume—P10 = 5.84 × 10⁷, P50 = 6.36 × 10⁷, P90 = 7.07 × 10⁷ m³; STOIIP—P10 = 1.58 × 10⁷, P50 = 1.72 × 10⁷, P90 = 1.91 × 10⁷ STB. The P10–P90 range (~18%) reflects realistic subsurface uncertainty rather than overly optimistic single-value estimates. The integrated workflow captures reservoir heterogeneity and delivers risk-aware P10/P50/P90 scenarios, supporting field-development decisions in deltaic margins analogous to Asian passive-margin settings.

abstracts.title: Global seafloor sediment mapping project
abstracts.text:
Modern seafloor sediments cover 70% of the Earth's surface, forming the substrate for the planet's largest ecosystem as well as one of its major carbon reservoirs. Seafloor sediment maps constitute fundamental marine geological datasets that document sediment distribution and transport, global biogeochemical cycles, metal deposit occurrences, and deep ocean current behaviour. However, existing global maps are hampered by inconsistent classification standards, limited access to historical data, and highly uneven spatial coverage. Therefore, a unified, observation based, and dynamically updatable global seafloor sediment map is essential to support marine geological research, resource assessment, offshore engineering, navigation, and ocean governance.

Building on robust regional research outcomes, we have published a series of 1:1,000,000 scale sediment type map for China's offshore seas (the Bohai Sea, Yellow Sea, East China Sea, and South China Sea), compiled from 26,235 stations. This mapping work is now being extended to the western Pacific, where more than 30,000 sediment stations are being collated and standardized. For this global project, we are systematically compiling, harmonizing, and performing quality control on both historical and newly acquired data, together with re-analysis of archived samples. Machine learning models will integrate validated observations with bathymetric data, seafloor geomorphology, and oceanographic parameters to predict substrate types and quantify mapping uncertainty. The resulting uncertainty maps highlight poorly constrained areas, guide targeted sampling campaigns, and support iterative refinement of models and substrate maps. We have joined scientists from various countries to launch the Global Seafloor Sediment Mapping Project, which will deliver an open access, interoperable, and continuously updatable global seafloor sediment map and associated database. It has been endorsed as a Decade Action under the UN Ocean Decade Programme "Digital Deep sea Typical Habitats", which provides an international framework for project implementation and collaboration.

abstracts.title: Oceanographic conditions off Tokai region under Kuroshio Current over the past 20,000 years
abstracts.text: The area off the Tokai region (33.5–34.5°N, 136.5–138.5°E) lies under the influence of the Kuroshio Current, which carries heat and moisture northward. Consequently, sea-surface temperature (SST) and water mass structure in this region, as well as precipitation over the adjacent land, are potentially sensitive to changes in Kuroshio transport strength and pathway. In this study, we measured Mg/Ca ratios and δ18O values of planktonic foraminifera shells from a sediment core collected off the Tokai region, central Japan, to understand the detailed evolution of oceanographic conditions for the past 20 kyr. We used sediment core KH16-6 St.2 PC (33.77°N, 137.61°E, 2250 m water depth) collected during the Hakuho Maru cruise. We analyzed δ18O values of both derived SST for G. ruber shows a gradual increase from the Last Glacial Maximum (LGM) to the Late Holocene, punctuated by distinct warming and cooling during the Bølling–Allerød (BA) and the Younger Dryas (YD), respectively. The δ18O values of G. ruber (surface) show variations corresponding to the BA and the YD, whereas those of G. inflata (sub-surface) do not. We further calculated the difference in δ18O values between the surface-and subsurface-dwelling species (Δδ18O) as an indicator of upper water column stratification. Δδ18O remained around –2.0‰ during the LGM and the late Holocene but shifted to significantly lower values of −2.5 to −3.0‰ during the Heinrich Stadial 1 (HS1) through the early Holocene. This pronounced decrease in Δδ18O likely reflects changes in surface water salinity, SST, and/or vertical mixing intensity, potentially driven by shifts in the Kuroshio pathway, transport strength, or other processes during the last deglaciation. In our presentation, we will compare these results with climate model simulations, and discuss the drivers underlying deglacial reorganization of upper water column stratification in the Kuroshio-dominated sector off the Tokai region, along with its potential link to precipitation variability.

abstracts.title: Inherited fault geometry and coupled surface processes control three-dimensional architecture of metamorphic core complexes
abstracts.text:
Metamorphic core complexes (MCCs) expose ductile mid- to lower-crustal rocks along large-offset, low-angle detachment faults. While the geometric diversity of MCCs, including whether their core domes are elongated parallel to the strike or the extension direction, is well documented, the governing mechanisms remain speculative. Here we used fully coupled three-dimensional geodynamic and landscape evolution models to investigate how inherited tectonic structures and surface processes control the development of individual domes and their periodic arrays. Our models simulating progressive normal-fault rotation showed that the undulating fault geometry imprints itself on the domes: a sinusoidal fault surface produces a periodic chain of domes, whereas a Gaussian one creates a prominent dome along the otherwise cylindrical fault. Increasing the amplitude of the undulating geometry elongates the domes parallel to the extension direction, and increasing the brittle thickness amplifies them in all dimensions.

Furthermore, surface processes including erosion and sedimentation promotes extension-parallel corrugations on the exhuming footwall. We suggest structural inheritance as the primary mechanism for the periodic chains of domes, the lateral variations in elongation orientation, and the extension-parallel drainage networks, observed in the Aegean Cyclades and the Woodlark Rift of Papua New Guinea. These findings highlight that both tectonic inheritance and surface processes are essential to the three-dimensional architecture of continental core complexes, providing a unified mechanical framework for the co-evolution of deep-crustal exhumation and surface landscape architecture.

abstracts.title: Coexisting regression and transgression in the Seomjin river estuary, southern Korea: Asynchronous Holocene evolution and spatial asymmetry
abstracts.text: Estuaries shows dynamic morphology and complex depositional patterns formed by the interaction of tidal and river processes. When interpreting tide-influenced estuary with spatially complex development, it is necessary to consider not only down-dip profiles reflecting transgressive–regressive phase in facies changes, but also along-strike variability to fully understand the evolution of the system. This study documents the sedimentary facies and stratigraphic architecture of the Seomjin River estuary, southern coast of Korea, where tidal and river processes interact. To build the Holocene stratigraphic architecture of the system, and to reconstruct the sedimentary evolution of the Seomjin River estuary, six borehole cores were obtained along both down-dip and along-strike transects, constrained by 77 radiocarbon and OSL ages for stratigraphic correlation and sedimentation-rate estimation. Based on facies analysis, the Holocene of the Seomjin River estuary deposits are classified into 23 sedimentary facies. The depositional succession is broadly divided into lower and upper units representing estuarine and deltaic facies during the Holocene. The estuarine facies show an upward-deepening succession from the tidal flat to bay mud deposits, followed by an upward-shallowing succession consisting of deltaic deposits. Multi-proxy analysis of sediment cores shows four depositional stages in terms of changes in sedimentary facies and sedimentation rate, suggesting a transition from estuary to delta. Between 10 and 8 ka BP, rapid transgression led to infilling of estuarine tidal flats, primarily along the margins of the estuary. From 8 to 4 ka BP, tidal influence remained significant, although the sedimentation rate slightly decreased. After 1.3 ka BP, frequent small-scale delta lobe switching occurred, leading to rapid infilling of the depocenter. In contrast, mud flat deposition continued along the estuarine margins under tidal influence. Such spatial variations in sequential development demonstrate that regression in the central estuary coexisted with continued transgression along the margins. This study signifies that contrasting facies architectures and evolutionary patterns can coexist along the down-dip and along-strike directions within a single estuarine system influenced by both tidal and fluvial processes.

abstracts.title: Holocene Fish Diversity and Shelf Development in the Taiwan Strait Based on Marine Sediment Cores
abstracts.text:
Postglacial sea-level rise transformed formerly exposed continental shelves into some of the world’s most productive marine ecosystems, yet the ecological development of these newly inundated landscapes remains poorly understood. Here, we reconstruct ~9,000 years of fish-community change in the Taiwan Strait using sedimentary otolith assemblages from two shallow (~60 m) marine sediment cores (Figure 1). A total of 818 otoliths were recovered, with 662 specimens identified to 90 taxa, documenting a diverse assemblage of mesopelagic, reef-associated, pelagic, demersal, and benthopelagic fishes. Sedimentary conditions influenced otolith recovery and taxonomic richness, but broad assemblage composition remained comparatively consistent between suitable core sites, supporting the use of sedimentary otoliths for paleoecological reconstruction in dynamic continental shelf settings.

Core S provides the most continuous temporal sequence. Although persistent marine deposition was established by ~9.0–8.3 ka cal BP, otolith accumulation rates and Hill diversity remained low for several millennia and increased only after ~5–4 ka. Both rose markedly after ~2.7–2.4 ka and remained elevated during the last ~2 ka, indicating the development of a more diverse and productive shelf fish community. These Late Holocene increases were robust across alternative 4–5 ka temporal cutoffs and persisted after accounting for chronological uncertainty and sedimentary conditions, although diversity was more sensitive to sediment sorting. The delayed ecological response following marine inundation is consistent with prolonged shelf stabilization and habitat development. These results extend sedimentary otolith paleoecology into shallow, dynamic continental-shelf environments along the Eurasian margin and provide a long-term ecological baseline for evaluating recent fisheries-driven change in the Taiwan Strait.

abstracts.title: Influence of a small mass-transport body on the development of adjacent channel systems in the deepwater Taranaki Basin
abstracts.text: The Neogene and Quaternary sedimentary succession in the deepwater Taranaki Basin, offshore NW New Zealand, is marked by high sedimentation rates (30 to 45 cm/kyr) and the development of various types of depositional elements including turbidity-current channel systems and mass transport deposits (MTDs). We use high-resolution (~7 m) 3D seismic data to investigate: (i) the origin and emplacement mechanism of a small (covering an area of ~1.18×108 m2) MTD named MTD-8 (Fig. 1; detached MTD style defined by Moscardelli & Wood, 2008) between horizons 15 and 16, and (ii) the influence of topography created by this MTD on the overlying depositional elements. Our results demonstrate that the MTD could be formed by partial collapse of the levee of an upslope channel (C-14C in Fig. 1). Underfilled erosional scars and protruding blocks are observed on top of MTD-8, which respectively generated negative and positive reliefs. The negative reliefs may redirect and focus the overlying channel (C-15D in Fig. 1) and promote avulsion of channel (type 1 of channel avulsion defined by Zhao et al. [2019]) on the outer bend near the headwall scarp of MTD-8. The positive reliefs on the toe region of MTD-8 may cause the bifurcation of the overlying channel (C-15D in Fig. 1). These observations show that even a relatively small MTD can reorganize subsequent deep-water channel pathways. These findings demonstrate the control of MTD-related topography on deep-water channel evolution and stratigraphic architecture.

abstracts.title: A tale of two water‑mass regimes: intraspecific morphometric divergence of Cycladophora davisiana (Radiolaria)
abstracts.text: Deep ventilation processes in the Northwest Pacific play a critical role in regulating global climate change and the carbon cycle. Radiolarians, as typical environmental indicator in subpolar regions, serves as an important tool for reconstructing the evolution of deep ventilation in the Northwest Pacific. A thorough understanding of radiolarian environmental implication is prerequisite for accurately interpreting past changes in radiolarian assemblages. Drawing upon the world atlas of Cycladophora davisiana distribution (Boltovskoy et al., 2010, we introduce a novel quantitative approach—C. davisiana morphometric parameters—providing, to our knowledge, the first C. davisiana species-specific size distributions.This study selects the Japan Sea (also known as the East Sea) and the Okhotsk Sea, which exhibit the highest abundances of the C. davisiana according to the latest compiled global dataset, to conduct morphometric comparisons of test length and width of C. davisiana from two depth-transects under significantly different water-mass regimes. The first species-specific morphometric analysis show C. davisiana sizes become larger in the Japan Sea with increasing water depth. Within the Okhotsk Sea, the Okhotsk Sea Intermediate Water, rather than the deep water, exhibits a distinctly larger C. davisiana sizes. The opposite size-depth trends point toward the influence of nutrient. Our results document intraspecific morphological divergence shaped by distinct hydrographic settings, yielding new insights into the environmental proxy significance of C. davisiana. Radiolarian morphometric parameters not only offer a potential quantitative approach for marine micropaleontological research but also hold promise for providing more robust evidence to reconstruct the evolution of deep ventilation in the Northwest Pacific since the Quaternary.

abstracts.title: Shifts in deep-sea fish communities across the last four superinterglacial intervals
abstracts.text: Fish production, diversity, and body size are sensitive to climate change, yet how fish communities respond to extreme warming and subsequently recover remains poorly understood over geological timescales. Past superinterglacials, when ocean temperatures exceeded Holocene levels, provide replicated natural experiments for evaluating ecological responses to warmer-than-present conditions. Here, we examine mesopelagic fish communities across four superinterglacial intervals identified in the western tropical Pacific record (Marine Isotope Stages 5e, 11c, 31, and 77), comparing pre-event, superinterglacial, and post-event phases. Fish production based on otolith accumulation rates and diversity decline consistently during these exceptionally warm intervals, followed by recovery as climate cools toward subsequent glacial conditions. Reconstructions of Myctophidae body size further suggest that superinterglacial assemblages differ in size structure from pre-event communities, with lower reconstructed individual biomass during superinterglacial phases, whereas post-event assemblages do not necessarily return immediately to the pre-event state. We therefore test whether this apparent size shift reflects size-selective ecological filtering, recruitment change, taxonomic turnover, or differential resilience among taxa and size classes. By combining reconstructed fish mass with otolith accumulation rates, we further evaluate a relative biomass-flux proxy that distinguishes changes in mean individual mass from changes in total biomass represented per unit time. Together, these repeated responses provide a framework for examining ecological reorganization after thermal thresholds are crossed and for quantifying the pace and completeness of recovery from extreme warming in pelagic and deep-sea fish communities.

abstracts.title: Quantifying millennial-scale coastal erosion and shore platform evolution using cosmogenic radionuclides and numerical models
abstracts.text:
Evaluating the long-term vulnerability of rocky coasts to sea-level rise requires accurate quantification of millennial-scale erosion and cliff retreat. This study integrates recently published cosmogenic radionuclide (10Be) exposure dating with process-based numerical modeling to reconstruct the long-term morphodynamics of rocky shorelines. Focusing on the Korean Peninsula, we examine how contrasting tectonic regimes and oceanographic conditions shape distinct coastal evolution patterns between the uplifting East Coast and the stable West Coast.

Our synthesis of 10Be concentrations reveals fundamentally different geomorphic trajectories across these end-members. On the microtidal, wave-dominated East Coast, platform morphology primarily reflects Holocene wave action, with cliff retreat rates showing site-specific variations—accelerating at Jangsa but decelerating at Ayajin and Jukbyeon-ri. In contrast, the macrotidal West Coast exhibits markedly elevated 10Be inventories across stepped platform topography (e.g., Kotji and Daehang-ri), confirming the preservation of multi-interglacial relict surfaces that serve as crucial archives of past sea-level stands.

These integrated observations and simulations illustrate the interactive roles of relative sea-level history, local wave energy, and regional vertical land motion in driving coastal cliff recession. By linking field-derived isotopic measurements with numerical modeling, this work couples model boundary conditions with time-dependent topographic shielding corrections derived from simulated cliff geometry, thereby enhancing our capacity to establish baseline erosion rates and predict future rocky coast hazards under accelerating global sea-level rise.

abstracts.title: Sediment provenance and dispersal pathways on the Heuksan Mud Belt, southwest Korean shelf: Insights from grain-size end-member analysis
abstracts.text: The provenance of fine-grained sediments of the Heuksan Mud Belt (HMB) on the southwest Korean shelf has remained controversial over the past two decades, particularly because of its large sediment volume and the potential contributions from both Korean and Chinese rivers. To better constrain sediment provenance and dispersal pathways, end-member analysis (EMA) was applied to grain-size distributions of 74 surface sediment samples across the HMB. Sedimentary facies analysis was additionally conducted to characterize the depositional processes responsible for sediment redistribution and accumulation. Five grain-size end-members (EMs) were identified, with dominant modes at 1.4 (EM1), 2.4 (EM2), 3.9 (EM3), 5.6 (EM4), and 7.3 ϕ (EM5). EM3 and EM4 occur predominantly on the inner shelf and decrease in abundance from proximal to distal areas. On the middle shelf, where tidal rhythmites occur, sediments are characterized by a mixture of EM4 and EM5, indicating a strong influence of tidal processes on sediment transport and redistribution. The contribution of EM4 progressively decreases offshore, whereas that of the finest end-member, EM5, increases toward the distal HMB. This systematic spatial transition reflects progressive grain-size sorting with increasing transport distance from the source. The spatial distributions and sorting patterns of EM4 and EM5 therefore suggest that these fine-grained components are predominantly derived from Korean rivers and subsequently dispersed offshore by tidal currents. Previous geochemical and clay-mineral studies, however, have suggested an additional contribution from Chinese rivers, particularly to the distal HMB. This apparent discrepancy indicates that sediment provenance inferred from grain-size distributions may reflect hydrodynamic sorting and redistribution as well as the original sediment source. Overall, the grain-size end-member approach provides new constraints on the provenance and dispersal pathways of sediments forming the HMB and highlights the important role of tidal processes in redistributing fine-grained sediments across the southwest Korean shelf. However, because the present study is based on surface sediments, it provides a snapshot of the modern sedimentary system. Further studies using deep-drill cores are therefore needed to reconstruct changes in sediment provenance during the Holocene and to clarify how variations in provenance and dispersal pathways have controlled the long-term evolution of the HMB.
