abstracts.title: Indian Ocean monsoon precipitation and the carbon cycle over the last 50,000 years
abstracts.text: The Indian Summer Monsoon profoundly influences the socio-economy of South Asia and regional biogeochemical cycles. Although marginal seas are key sinks for global organic carbon burial, the mechanisms by which the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation drives ISM variability via teleconnections on millennial scales, and how marginal sea carbon sinks respond to the nonlinear coupling of sea level and monsoon, remain debated. Focusing on deep-sea sediment core YDY09 from the central Bay of Bengal, this study established a high-resolution chronostratigraphic framework for the last 50 ka. By integrating environmental magnetism, geochemical multi-proxy analyses, and iTRACE transient climate simulations, we reconstructed the evolutionary history of the paleomonsoon and the sedimentary carbon cycle. The results indicate: (1) Climate Driving Mechanisms: The ISM precipitation exhibits a characteristic pattern of "weakening during Heinrich Stadials (HS) and strengthening during the Bølling-Allerød warm period." Simulation results reveal that AMOC weakening does not control the monsoon solely through the southward shift of the Intertropical Convergence Zone. Instead, it induces an Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD)-like sea surface temperature pattern, triggering an anticyclonic circulation over the northern Indian Ocean. This circulation hinders moisture transport to the Indian subcontinent, acting as the dominant factor for monsoon failure during HS events. (2) Sedimentary and Carbon Cycle Responses: The Bay of Bengal demonstrates a unique "sea-level driven" mode. Distinct from the Arabian Sea, which is primarily controlled by monsoon-induced upwelling, the low sea level during the Last Glacial Maximum (LGM) in the Bay of Bengal facilitated a direct connection between the river mouth and submarine canyons, leading to rapid transport of massive terrigenous detritus to the deep sea. While this high-flux input accelerated material cycling, it exerted a strong "dilution effect" on authigenic organic carbon, resulting in significantly reduced organic carbon burial during the LGM.

abstracts.title: Transport and depositional processes of terrigenous organic matter to deep sea sediments in the Bengal Fan
abstracts.text:
The Bengal Fan in northeastern Indian Ocean is a submarine fan formed by transport of huge clastic sediments by the confluent Ganges and the Brahmaputra rivers attributed to the India–Asia collision and uplift of the Himalayas and the Tibetan Plateau (e.g., Curray et al., 2003). Terrigenous organic matter transported far offshore from river mouths is deposited in the Bengal Fan (Lee et al., 2019). Quantitative analyses can assess the input of terrestrial materials into the ocean and their role in the carbon cycle. In the present study, we analyzed biomarkers, minerals, and microfossils in sediment core from the Bengal Fan to evaluate its sedimentary system.

We used the sediment cores recovered at Site U1444 (Bengal Fan) by Integrated Ocean Drilling Program (IODP) Expedition 353. The ages were determined by microfossil stratigraphy, and the lowermost horizon was estimated to be about 6 Ma. Core U1444A is composed of 4 sedimentary facies; Unit 1 consists of silty sand and silty clay with thick turbidites, and Units 2–4 contain clay, silty sand, and clayey silt with thin turbidites. We sampled and analyzed separately the coarse-grained layers, and the fine-grained layers just above and below the coarse-grained layers (just above: turbidite mud (Tmud), just below: hemipelagite) in turbiditic sequences. The grain-size distribution and composition of the sediment particles were determined by microscopic observation of smear slides. Freeze-dried sediments were extracted by solvents and then separated into fractions by silica-gel column. These fractions were analyzed by GC-MS.

Quartzes, feldspars, calcareous nannofossils, and wood were mainly contained in sediments of U1444 core. Steroids and terrestrial plant-derived terpenoids (TPTs) were mainly detected in the sediments. Overall, high proportions of minerals, wood, and TPTs in Unit 1. In Units 2 and 4, the coarse-grained layers exhibited a marked increase in mean grain size and a high proportion of minerals, but biomarker indicators showed various trends. The data for minerals, microfossils, and biomarkers reveal two distinct patterns: one is characterized by lower TPT concentrations in the coarse-grained layers than in the fine-grained layers, and a higher ratio of dehydroabietic acid (DAA; conifer biomarker). These results suggest that DAA contained in more refractory resins and wood might be redeposited by submarine landslides. Whereas, the other is characterized by high abundances of TPTs in the coarse-grained layers. These results suggest that terrigenous materials were efficiently transported to the Bengal Fan through multiple sources and processes.

abstracts.title: Biomarker-derived temperatures and paleoenvironmental changes in the Korea Gap (Ulleung Basin), East Sea since the last glacial period
abstracts.text: The Korea Gap is a deep passage in the East Sea, connecting the Ulleung Basin with Japan Basin and playing a key role in seawater exchange between the two basins. Despite its oceanographic importance and several investigations, biomarker records, particularly glycerol dialkyl glycerol tetraethers (GDGTs) and alkenones, from this region remain scarce. Here, we report GDGT and alkenone concentrations in piston core 05GCRP-17, recovered from the Korea Gap at a water depth of 2,405 m, and evaluated proxy-derived temperature signals and their paleoenvironmental implications. The core sediments consist mainly of pelagic and hemipelagic mud with intercalated turbidites, Mn-carbonate mud, and volcanic tephra layers. The age–depth model, based on eight AMS Sea, indicates that the core 05GCRP-17 extends to approximately 35 ka. GDGT and alkenone concentrations were generally high within turbidite layers, whereas GDGT- and alkenone-based indices (e.g., BIT, %GDGT-0, GDGT-2/GDGT-3, TEX86L, U%& intervals. GDGT-derived temperatures varied from 5.3 to 17.4°C and showed pronounced variability during deglaciation, followed by an overall increasing trend through the Holocene. On the other hand, alkenone-derived temperatures varied from 11.0 to 20.8°C, with the highest value occurring during the last glacial period, followed by pronounced fluctuations during deglaciation and an overall increase through the Holocene. However, alkenone-derived temperatures were not reliable during the last glacial interval because alkenone abundances were too low for robust index determination. Downcore variations in GDGT-derived indices were particularly more marked than that of alkenone. The divergence between the two proxy records, particularly during deglaciation, implies that GDGT- and alkenone-derived temperatures did not respond identically to environmental changes. This discrepancy may reflect differences in the seasonality and/or depth of biomarker production, in addition to changes in seawater temperatures. Thus, the two biomarker records likely capture different components of the evolving upper-ocean environment in the Korea Gap. Nonetheless, our results demonstrate that biomarker records in the Korea Gap provide important constraint on paleoenvironmental and inter-basin oceanographic changes in the East Sea since the last glacial period.

abstracts.title: Distinguishing complex sedimentary processes on the southeastern continental shelf of Korea using surface sediment grain-size characteristics
abstracts.text: This study applies End-Member Analysis (EMA) to surface-sediment grain-size distributions on the southeastern continental shelf of Korea, where the Korea Strait Shelf Mud (KSSM) occurs. In addition, depositional processes and sediment origins were identified based on the spatial patterns and interrelationships of grain-size characteristics, including sortable silt mean size (S̅S̅) and percentage (SS%). Four End-Members (EMs) were identified. Characterized by the finest mean grain size (Mz), EM1 (Mz = 4.4 μm) occurred at high proportions on the northern continental slope, the deepest part of the study area. Its proportion also increased offshore, indicating that EM1 represents background sediment of aeolian origin supplied to the East Sea. EM2 (Mz = 9.3 μm) generally occurred at high proportions on the inner shelf at water depths shallower than 100 m. Its proportion was highest within the KSSM, which develops along the coastline under the influence of the northward-flowing Korea Coastal Current (KCC), indicating that EM2 represents Nakdong River-derived muddy sediment. In contrast, coarse-grained EM3 (Mz = 174.4 μm) and EM4 (Mz = 332.6 μm) were concentrated on the outer shelf and were interpreted as relict sediments formed during past sea-level lowstands. Their contrasting spatial distributions likely reflect shifts in paleoshoreline position associated with transgression. In addition to EMA, the relationships among S̅S̅, SS% and clay content also allowed different sorting processes to be distinguished. The sediments were divided into three groups: inner-shelf mud influenced by selective deposition, outer-shelf sand influenced by winnowing, and mixed sediments composed of the two sediment groups. Such classification can help identify the types of hydrodynamic sorting processes affecting the sediments and may provide a broadly applicable criterion across diverse marine environments.

abstracts.title: Re-evaluating the radiogenic neodymium signature of North Pacific Intermediate Water: New insights from authigenic phases in Okhotsk Sea sediments
abstracts.text: Tracing the evolution of North Pacific Intermediate/Deep Water formation is critical for understanding global climate dynamics. However, some biological isotopic proxies (e.g., δ13C, 14C) are often constrained by carbonate scarcity and anomalously 14C-depleted geologic carbon input in the Northwest Pacific. In contrast, authigenic εNd serves as a robust tracer independent of biological processes, but its application in the volcanically active Northwest Pacific is complicated by reactive volcanic influence. Here, we systematically evaluated the effects of leaching parameters, including acetic acid (HAc) and hydroxylamine hydrochloride (HH) concentrations, EDTA, and leaching duration, on the extraction of authigenic εNd from Northwest Pacific sediments. Our results show that higher HAc concentration and EDTA addition significantly improve Nd recovery. Geochemical indicators demonstrate that the optimized leaching protocol–a 10-minute leach with 0.25 M HAc, 0.005 M HH, and 0.003 M EDTA–preferentially extracts the dominant authigenic Fe-Mn phase with minimal detrital contamination. Applying this protocol to intermediate-depth sediments from the Okhotsk Sea reveals a significant positive correlation between authigenic and detrital εNd. This relationship suggests that the authigenic εNd signal acquires a distinct radiogenic fingerprint during early diagenesis through interaction with reactive volcanic materials likely derived from the Okhotsk-Chukotka volcanic belt and the Kamchatka Peninsula. Furthermore, authigenic εNd values display a northeast-to-southwest gradient, and the value from the southwestern Okhotsk Sea is consistent with the average filtered North Pacific Intermediate Water (NPIW) signature from the Northwest Pacific north of 40°N. This agreement suggests that the εNd signature of NPIW may retain an early-diagenetic imprint acquired in the Okhotsk Sea, supporting the use of authigenic εNd to trace NPIW formation and transport pathways. This finding provides new insight into the definition of NPIW εNd end-members for water-mass mixing models, indicating that the influence of source-region diagenetic modification on water-mass εNd signatures should be considered. This mechanism may also explain the radiogenic nature of NPIW relative to Pacific Deep Water.

abstracts.title: Typhoon- and earthquake-triggered turbidity current activities over the past 4000 years in the Gaoping Submarine Canyon of the northeastern South China Sea
abstracts.text:
Submarine canyons are the principal conduits for turbidity currents transporting sediments to the deep sea. Turbidites, as sedimentary products of turbidity currents, are believed to bear abundant information on global and regional climatic and tectonic histories and are widely used to study triggering mechanisms of turbidity currents and to reconstruct paleoenvironmental changes. The Gaoping Submarine Canyon, located off southwest Taiwan and in the northeastern South China Sea, is featured with steep topography, active seismicity, and high terrigenous sediment flux. Previous studies recognized turbidites well preserved in the Gaoping Submarine Canyon but their triggered mechanisms need further explored. This study realizes high-resolution grain-size (1 cm) along with clay mineral (10 cm) measurements at Core MD18-3565 (19.68 m long = 3954 cal yr BP) to investigate the provenance of turbidites and triggering mechanisms of turbidity currents in the Gaoping Submarine Canyon during the late Holocene.

The results show that a total number of 318 turbidite layers (>0.1 cm thick) occurred over the past ~4000 years in the Gaoping Submarine Canyon. Clay mineralogy identifies the Gaoping river in southwestern Taiwan as the predominant source of sediments in the turbidite layers. Grain size distribution characteristics show types A– D as typical coarse-grain turbidite layers. Probability cumulative curves of these turbidite layers (Types A–D) present two-level/mixed saltation populations for Type C, which are characteristics of proximal turbidity activities. C-M double logarithmic scatter plot indicating typical turbidites for Types A/B and C layers (parallel to C=M), showing two driven mechanisms of turbidity current activities, i.e., typhoon- and earthquake-triggered events. Frequency and probability cumulative distribution of grain size are utilized to distinguish turbidites triggered by typhoons and earthquakes, through their coarse trailing tail and two-level/mixed saltation populations. This study highlights that over the past ~4000 yrs in the Gaoping submarine canyon, long-term variations of typhoon-triggered turbidity activities are closely related to millennium-scale ENSO activities, while earthquake-triggered turbidite activities show active tectonics during 3100-3400 yrs BP around Taiwan.

abstracts.title: Divergent temperature changes between surface and intermediate waters in the southern South China Sea since the last deglaciation
abstracts.text:
The intermediate water serves as a critical medium between sea surface and deep waters, playing a central role in marine heat exchange and the carbon cycle (Giering et al., 2014; Wang et al., 2023). A cooling trend has been documented in intermediate water of the northern South China Sea (nSCS) since the Last Glacial Maximum (LGM), attributed to temperature changes in Pacific intermediate water (Yang et al., 2020; Ali et al., 2025). However, how intermediate water temperature (IWT) in the southern SCS (sSCS) evolved remains unclear—a gap crucial for understanding heat-exchange mechanisms in the SCS.

Here we reconstruct IWT using branched glycerol dialkyl glycerol tetraethers (brGDGTs) from two sediment cores(MD05-2892 and 18252-3) spanning the last 21 kyr in the sSCS. From the LGM to the Holocene, brGDGT sources shifted from terrestrial-dominated to marine-dominated with rising sea levels. The IWT reconstructed from marine-derived brGDGTs shows a cooling trend from the late deglaciation to the Holocene, in anti-phase with surface and subsurface temperature changes. This trend is consistent with nSCS records, supporting SCS basin overturning circulation—rather than changes in Pacific intermediate water—as the primary driver of IWT variation.

From the late deglaciation to the Holocene, the temperature difference (ΔT) between intermediate and surface waters increased, indicating enhanced water column stratification. Both the branched and isoprenoid tetraether (BIT) index and brGDGT concentration decreased with increasing ΔT, suggesting reduced export productivity, weakened heterotrophic microbial respiration, and decreased dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC) storage in intermediate waters—potentially representing a positive feedback to concurrent atmospheric CO₂ rise.

abstracts.title: Depth-dependent chlorine cycling at the magmatic-hydrothermal interface of mid-ocean ridges: Insights from hornfelsic diabase
abstracts.text: The conductive boundary layer (CBL) at the magmatic-hydrothermal interface of mid-ocean ridges (MORs) regulates heat and chemical exchange between cooling magmas and circulating seawater. While well-documented at shallow, fast-spreading ridges, this interface remains poorly constrained in deep-seated magmatic environments such as slow-spreading oceanic core complexes (OCCs). Here, we show that hornfelsic diabase from the Onnuri OCC (Central Indian Ridge) exhibits remarkably low chlorine (Cl) signatures in both amphiboles (< 663 ppm) and fluid inclusions (2.0–5.0 wt.% NaCl eq.), contrasting sharply with the high-Cl brines typical of shallow fast-spreading systems. We demonstrate that this divergence stems from the pressure-regulated phase behavior of seawater: high hydrostatic pressure suppresses phase separation and prevents the formation of a basal brine layer, whereas low pressure facilitates brine accumulation. A meta-analysis of global MORB chemistry and hydrothermal vent datasets confirms that magma storage depth—driven by segment-scale magmatic flux— exerts ultimate control over crustal Cl assimilation and vent fluid stability. We propose a unified, depth-dependent model for MOR Cl cycling, concluding that heat source emplacement depth dictates the hydrostatic pressure of the hydrothermal cell, thereby controlling subseafloor brine formation, magmatic Cl contamination, and hydrothermal vent fluid dynamics globally (Fig. 1). Furthermore, this depth-dependent model provides fundamental insights into hydrothermal metal mobilization: while shallow circulation induces vigorous phase separation and yields Cl-poor vapor that restricts the transport of chloride-complexed metals to the seafloor, deep circulation sustains single-phase conditions that facilitate steady, uniform metal chloride complexation and fluid mobility throughout the upflow zone (Fig. 1)—a hypothesis that warrants evaluation in future studies.

abstracts.title: How data sets of marine sedimentation better support system modelling for climate change studies
abstracts.text: GCMs (General Circulation Models) used to be the physical basis for climate modelling in atmospheric science. When the temporal and spatial scales are expanded towards “deep time”, however, it is insufficient to merely use the atmospheric physics and the associated big data in the modelling. The climate models, as a component of the earth system model, will depend on a range of data sources, which will fundamentally change the way of modelling research. Marine sedimentation contains information on different climate zones, records the time series of climate changes, and reveals process-product relationships. The diversity of the data sets is significant: the material property analysis from grain size, mineralogy to geochemical composition, biological fossils, and spatial distribution patterns and scales of the sedimentary body, are common examples. Traditionally, these materials are analysed to obtain climate proxies, to reveal climate changes. Nowadays, in the age of new GCMs (Global Climate Models) incorporating systems theory and AI techniques, the research efficiency will be greatly enhanced: the sediment data can be used to search possible climate conditions that are responsible, or the climate conditions can be used as model input to search possible consequences as sediment deposits. For instance, while the information on climate conditions may be obtained by a study of the formation of coastal chenier systems, it is also the case that the characteristics of the chenier systems may be revealed by an evaluation of the climate conditions. It is worth noting that when multiple effects stem from a single cause, inferring climatic characteristics and seeking the relevant evidence from sedimentary features is more challenging than deducing sedimentary features and finding supporting evidence from climatic characteristics. The difficulty levels of these two analytical processes are asymmetric. Climate system simulations supported by AI may achieve higher efficiency by adopting the latter approach. Thus, within the new framework of system models, the marine sedimentary should be re-examined, to identify more information on climate change patterns.

abstracts.title: Marine gold placer deposits in Semangko Bay – Lampung – south Sumatra, Indonesia
abstracts.text: This research is based on the consideration that primary gold deposits in coastal areas have undergone processes of denudation, transportation and deposition resulting in their distribution in shallow marine waters around the adjacent terrestrial gold deposits. To prove this hypothesis, a total of 153 seabed sediment samples were systematically taken at 1 km intervals so that the distribution of placer gold in the sea could be systematically mapped. The maximum sampling depth was 50 m, adjusted to the capabilities of the dredger fleet owned by PT Timah, which is considered capable of exploiting these valuable metal deposits. Furthermore, 16 coastal sediment samples were also taken to determine the distribution of secondary gold along the coast. The analytical results obtained gold content values ranging from 0.01 to 0.63 grams per ton, with the highest concentration pattern found in the southeastern part of Semangko Bay near the primary deposit sources in the coastal area. This selected area has prospects for further development. The resource estimation from this research obtained potential measured resources of approximately 4 tons of secondary gold below the seafloor of Semangko Bay.

abstracts.title: Toward resolving MIS 3 sea level changes: Regional GIA dynamics in the epicontinental Yellow Sea
abstracts.text:
A long-standing enigma for sea level studies is constraining ice-sheet volume over the last ice age, particularly during Marine Isotope Stage 3 (MIS 3; 57-29 ka), which has been challenged by data scarcity. Legacy sea level records can be contaminated by process that change their vertical elevation, including tectonics, glacial isostatic adjustment (GIA), sediment loading, and compaction. Although the Yellow Sea has been regarded as a favorable ‘far-field’ setting (distance from formerly glaciated region) for reconstructing global mean sea level (GMSL), owing to minimal GIA-induced deviation from the global signal, yet the magnitude and spatial variability of its regional GIA response during MIS 3 remain poorly constrained.

Here we discuss existing observation inference of MIS 3 relative sea level (RSL) and show how our new OSL-dated tidal sea level index point (SLIP) from southwestern Korea provides additional insight to resolving MIS 3 sea level. We perform a suite of GIA simulations using 3 global ice histories and 12 viscoelastic Earth models to predict site-specific RSL. We then compare these predictions to a compilation of MIS 3 sea level data. Notably, our RSL prediction consistently shows a north-south RSL gradient across the Yellow Sea, with deviation from GMSL of up to ~16 m, indicating an amplified continental levering effect across the epicontinental shelf. Moreover, the magnitude of the predicted GIA signal is strongly dependent on the adopted ice history, with differences of up to ~8 m. This suggests that, despite its far-field setting, the Yellow Sea is not immune from GIA. By integrating the GIA ensemble and its model uncertainty, we provide new constraints on MIS 3 GMSL that fall above most previous oxygen isotope-based and GIA-based reconstruction. Our findings show that regional GIA dynamics can substantially reshape the RSL signal from far-field sedimentary records and further provide a boundary condition for evaluating ice-sheet reconstruction.

abstracts.title: The importance of terrestrial outcrops for reconstructing marine paleoenvironments using the alkenone paleothermometer
abstracts.text:
Alkenones, C37-alkylketones produced by the haptophyte phytoplankton Gephyrocapsa oceanica, paleoceanography. Most alkenone-based paleotemperature studies have relied on deep-sea core sediments where organic molecules are well preserved. Terrestrial outcrops, however, offer several advantages for paleoenvironmental reconstruction: they provide large, repeatable sample volumes and allow construction of composite sections that can compensate for stratigraphic gaps, and they often host well-developed paleontological and microfossil stratigraphic records based on traditional studies. At the same time, outcrop materials are subject to weathering and diagenetic alteration, and consequently alkenone-based studies using terrestrial samples remain relatively scarce (e.g. Kajita et al., 2022).

In this study we examined Neogene and Quaternary strata exposed in Kanazawa City, Ishikawa Prefecture, Japan, assessing organic maturity indices and the presence of alkenones, and performed preliminary sea-surface temperature (SST) estimates. The Quaternary Omma Formation, summarized by Kitamura (2016), preserves clear depositional cycles and molluscan assemblage changes interpreted as glacial–interglacial oscillations. At the type locality Saigawa section, large SST variations interpreted as glacial–interglacial shifts were recorded, ranging from 16.5 to 26.8 ℃. Many stratigraphic levels corresponding to glacial intervals, however, lack alkenone records because fine, mud-sized particles were not deposited. Alkenones were also recovered from stratigraphically lower units—the Asagaya, Yamashina, Saigawa, and Koderayama formations. The lowermost Asagaya Formation corresponds to the Middle Miocene Climatic Optimum (MMCO; ~15.9 Ma) and consists of sedimentary rocks deposited at very high rates exceeding 1000 m/myr that could allow ultra-high-resolution investigations at sub-centennial (i.e., <1,000 year) timescales. The detection of substantial amounts of ββ-homohopanes indicates extremely low thermal maturity, confirming that alkenone-based paleotemperature reconstruction is feasible for these rocks. Reconstructed SSTs from these samples are generally ≥24.3 ℃, and some samples exceed the upper evaluation limit for the alkenone proxy (27.4 ℃). These results are consistent with previous paleontological interpretations for shallower strata distributed in the Hokuriku Region in Japan.

Our results demonstrate that the Neogene–Quaternary strata around Kanazawa are particularly immature from an organic-geochemical perspective and are well suited for alkenone biomarker investigations. We propose extending alkenone-based SST measurements across the Hokuriku region to supplement traditional micropaleontological, qualitative environmental interpretations with quantitative paleotemperature data, thereby enabling more detailed regional paleoenvironmental reconstructions.

abstracts.title: Microbial reduction and transformation of deep sea vernadite by Shewanella oneidensis MR-1
abstracts.text:
Marine ferromanganese deposits, such as crusts and nodules, are widespread on the seafloor and host diverse microbial communities. While the role of microbes in the formation of these manganese oxides is recognized, their influence on the subsequent alteration and reduction of these minerals, particularly in environments like oxygen minimum zone (OMZ), remains poorly understood. This study investigates the anaerobic reduction and subsequent mineral phase transition of seafloor vernadite mediated by the metal-reducing bacterium Shewanella oneidensis MR-1.

We conducted batch experiment using natural vernadite obtained from a hydrogenetic Fe-Mn crust. The experiments were divided into three anoxic groups: Live Cell, Heat-Killed Cell, and an Abiotic control using a chemical reducing agent (Na-dithionite). Aqueous concentrations of dissolved Mn and Fe were monitored over time using ICP-OES, and solid phase mineralogical changes were analyzed using Raman spectroscopy and X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy (XPS).

The aqueous phase results revealed that the live cell group show exhibited the fastest and most dominant Mn reduction. Notably, the heat-killed group also induced significant reduction distinct from the abiotic control, indicating that biologically induced reactions-likely mediated by microbial exudates such as extracellular polymeric substances (EPS) or ligands -play a critical role alongside active microbial metabolism. Solid-phase analyses demonstrated a clear two-step mineralogical transformation across all microbially influenced groups. Raman spectra indicated the structural rearrangement of layered vernadite into tunnel-structured todorokite. Subsequently, solution-mediated re-precipitation occurred, forming Mn(III) oxide minerals, which was confirmed by a Mn 3s doublet energy separation of 5.4 eV in the XPS analysis.

These findings suggest that deep-sea Mn oxides are not static geological entities but undergo continuous, dynamic biogeochemical cycling driven by both active microbial metabolism and biogenic products. Understanding these pathways provides critical insights into interpreting seafloor mineral system and paleoceanographic proxies.

abstracts.title: Holocene Arabian Sea stratification and deoxygenation in response to monsoon weakening
abstracts.text: Seasonal stratification in the Arabian Sea, driven by the Indian summer monsoon, fuels one of the planet’s most productive marine ecosystems while intensifying one of the largest oxygen minimum zones—an interplay with profound implications for biogeochemical cycles. Despite its central role in regional climate and food security across South Asia, the summer monsoon long-term influence on upper-ocean stratification and oxygenation remains uncertain. Here we present century-scale sea-surface temperature reconstructions and multiproxy evidence for Arabian Sea warming (~1.4 ± 0.4 °C) across the Holocene. We find that stronger summer monsoon winds during the early Holocene (~10–6 thousand years ago) enhanced vertical mixing, whereas subsequent monsoon weakening and surface-warming increased stratification and reduced ventilation. Multiproxy indicators reveals progressive deoxygenation across the Holocene. Our findings indicate that both past and projected warming have progressively intensified upper-ocean stratification, fueling further expansion of the Arabian Sea oxygen minimum zone.

abstracts.title: Origin of chlorite in sediment from the Cheoeum Vent Field, an inactive hydrothermal system on the central Indian Ridge
abstracts.text: A distinct greenish-gray sediment patch was discovered during an ROV survey at the Cheoeum Vent Field (CVF), an inactive hydrothermal site on the Central Indian Ridge (CIR). In hydrothermal environments, authigenic minerals form and undergo alteration processes through water-rock interactions, recording changes in depositional conditions and fluid composition through time. To investigate origin and depositional environment of sediments, a push core was recovered from approximately 3,070 m water depth using a push corer. Mineralogical composition was determined by X-ray diffraction (XRD), and clay mineral chemistry was characterized by scanning electron microscopy with energy dispersive spectroscopy (SEM-EDS). Bulk geochemical composition and rare earth element (REE) concentrations were analyzed to calculate the metalliferous sediment index (MSI) and chondrite-normalized REE patterns. The sediment was dominated by talc and chlorite, with MSI values consistently below 0.4, confirming a hydrothermal origin. XRD analysis of the <2 µm fraction identified the Ⅱb type chlorite, consistent with hydrothermal alteration. In contrast to the positive Eu anomaly typically reported for hydrothermal sediments, the chondrite-normalized REE patterns showed a negative Eu anomaly, indicating seawater overprinting after hydrothermal activity ceased. The negative Eu anomaly likely resulted from the oxidation of Eu2+, released during hydrothermal mineral dissolution, to Eu3+ under oxic conditions, followed by redistribution with other REEs. Ferrihydrite occurrence in the sediments further supports the interpretation of seawater overprinting and REE redistribution. In addition, chlorite exhibited Mg enrichment, suggesting the influence of seawater and hydrothermal fluids on the sediments. Chlorite geothermometry based on its chemical composition was applied to estimate the formation temperature. Formation temperatures decreased upward through the core, from an average of 208 ℃ to below approximately <~40 ℃ at the top, reflecting a progressive weakening of hydrothermal activity over time. These results demonstrate that chlorite mineralogy and geothermometry serve as effective proxies for reconstructing the depositional and thermal history of inactive hydrothermal vent fields.

abstracts.title: Carbonate and organic carbon deposition in the Surveyor Fan (IODP Site U1417) in the Gulf of Alaska (northeast Pacific) during the late Miocene to early Pleistocene
abstracts.text: Carbonate and organic carbon deposition in deep-sea fan sediments play a key role in sequestering carbon through diverse pathways and reactions within the marine carbon cycle. International Ocean Discovery Program (IODP) Site U1417, located in the Surveyor Fan (Gulf of Alaska), preserves hemipelagic sediments influenced by glacial and fluvial depositional processes from the Cordilleran Ice Sheet in the Chugach–St. Elias Mountains and Coastal Mountains. IODP Site U1417 was drilled at five holes (A, B, C, D, and E), and more than 400 sediment samples from Holes U1417D and U1417E were used in this study. The age model of IODP Site U1417 was constructed on board by integrating magnetostratigraphy and biostratigraphy based on diatoms, radiolarians, and foraminifera, showing ~9 Ma sedimentary record, and the studied interval covers the late Miocene to early Pleistocene. Although the lithostratigraphic boundaries are usually gradational, five lithostratigraphic units (I–V) were defined based on the lithofacies associations, with further subunits in unit I (IA and IB) and unit V (VA to VJ). All the analytical data do now show distinct glacial–interglacial change mainly due to the low sampling resolution. CaCO3 content was remarkably low (mostly less than 5%) throughout the whole interval, which is attributed mainly to poor carbonate preservation due to the deep water depth (~4,200 m) at drilling site close to the carbonate compensation depth. However, markedly higher concentrations (occasionally more than 20% and up to 60%) occurred intermittently, indicating that CaCO3 content is not associated with depositional processes. The stable δ13C and δ18O values (~–21.6‰ and ~+4.9‰, respectively) of these carbonates reflect the influence of methane, suggesting that the carbonate deposition records the postdepostional formation of methane-derived inorganic carbonates through porewater geochemical reactions including anaerobic oxidation of methane. The downcore variations between biogenic opal and total organic carbon (TOC) contents seem opposite: diatom-rich intervals are characterized by high biogenic opal (~10%) and low TOC (~0.3%) contents and vice versa. In general, the biogenic opal deposition attributed to the degree of diatom production led to the TOC deposition on the seafloor. However, in the Surveyor Fan, intervals dominated by terrigenous sediments contain higher TOC content (~0.6%). Based on the relationship between TOC and C/N ratio as well as δ13C values of sediment organic carbon, TOC content in clast-rich terrigenous intervals is more influenced by terrestrial organic carbon. In the presentation, we will figure out the organic carbon deposition quantitatively between the diatom-bearing clay-rich intervals and clast-rich terrigenous intervals for the carbon storage history in the deep sea fan system.

abstracts.title: Recent advances and applications of drill coring in ferromanganese crust exploration and research
abstracts.text: Recently, drill-core sampling has become indispensable in ferromanganese (Fe-Mn) crust research and exploration as objectives have evolved from simple occurrence verification to detailed stratigraphic interpretation, paleoceanographic reconstruction, and quantitative resource evaluation. Compared to traditional dredge samples from early reconnaissance surveys, drill cores offer precise geographic and bathymetric control while maintaining the intact crust-substrate boundary. This presentation reviews the historical development and modern applications of drill coring for Fe-Mn deposits, highlighting its critical role in advancing future deep-sea research and resource assessments across local and regional scales.

abstracts.title: Urbino Summer School in Paleoclimatology 2026: Framework, participation experience, and benefit towards greater paleoclimate research
abstracts.text:
The Urbino Summer School in Paleoclimatology 2026 (USSP 2026) is one of a few summer schools sponsored by the European Consortium of Ocean Research Drilling (ECORD), with the goal of further equipping young researchers with skills and knowledge relating to marine-related science, and their applications in ocean-drilling related science such as IODP3.

USSP 2026 was held in Urbino, Italy, and brought together 54 young researchers from various institutions across Europe, the Americas and Japan. The participants also ranged from various backgrounds, such as climatic modellers involved in methane budgets, geochemists involved in foraminifera or lipid-biomarker based paleoenvironmental reconstruction, paleobotanists involved in terrestrial paleoclimate reconstruction, as well as paleomagnetologists and cyclostratigraphers involved in decoding astronomical phenomenas.

Additionally, instructors from different fields also came for a few days to give lectures on their specialties and to discuss our own research. The lecture topics, which ended with classroom exercises, included topics within Earth’s many systems (i.e. carbon cycle, water cycle, etc.), cyclostratigraphy, geochemical proxies and statistical analysis, as well as cryospheric sciences and climatic modelling. A field work to outcrops exposing important global climatic phenomenas was also conducted, and we got to see sedimentary layers belonging to the Ocean Anoxic Events 1 and 2, the Cretaceous-Paleogene extinction event, as well as the Paleocene-Eocene Thermal Maximum. Everyone also gave a poster presentation, while some of us also gave an oral presentation on our current research.

Additional lectures on Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DEI) as well as recent developments in IODP3 (including SPARCs and Japan’s ReCoRD) were given. Apart from USSP, other summer schools, including Japan’s upcoming Kochi Core School 2026, were also introduced.

Participation in USSP not only broadened my knowledge on paleoclimate, but it also allowed me to see how my own research can be beneficial to fields that appear unrelated to my own. And most important of all, participation in USSP allowed me to connect and network with researchers from many different sub-fields under paleoclimate. I feel like in a time where inter-disciplinary research is becoming more necessary, and in a time where inter-connections and teleconnections are becoming more apparent, such a wide variety of potential collaborators is needed.

This presentation at ICMAG-10 will talk about the general framework of USSP, my participation experience and what I’ve gained as a participant. A brief introduction to funding opportunities used to participate in USSP 2026 will also be given.

abstracts.title: Suspended sediment plume dynamics around the Ieodo Ocean Research Station: Preliminary Results
affiliations: Department of Ocean Sciences, Inha University, Incheon 22212, Republic of Korea
Korea Hydrographic and Oceanographic Agency, Busan 49111, Republic of Korea
School of Earth and Environmental Sciences, Seoul National University, Seoul 08826, Republic of Korea
Department of Civil, Urban, Earth, and Environmental Engineering, Ulsan National Institute of Science and Technolog, Ulsan 44919 Republic of Korea
abstracts.text: Suspended sediment plumes are produced where turbulence is enhanced by the interaction of ocean currents with bottom topography. Around offshore structures, turbulence is further intensified as the flow is redirected into downflow and horseshoe vortices, promoting local scour and resuspension. Despite the significance of these plumes for sediment transport around offshore platforms, in-situ observations of their formation and evolution have rarely been reported. In this study, suspended sediment plumes around the Ieodo Ocean Research Station (I-ORS), situated on Ieodo seamount approximately 150 km southwest of Jeju Island, Korea, were investigated. The plumes were analyzed using multispectral satellite imagery (November 2015–August 2026) and in-situ measurements. Of the 198 cloud-free scenes examined, plumes were identified in 96 scenes using a Gaussian Mixture Model, and plume orientation was quantified by principal component analysis. The seamount summit was identified as the dominant plume source, and the plume orientation aligned with the prevailing tidal current at the time of image acquisition, most often northwestward. Plume signatures near I-ORS in the satellite imagery were close to the detection limit, and in-situ observations were therefore employed to resolve these features. During a field survey from 14 to 17 May 2026, two plume sources, one associated with the seamount summit and the other with I-ORS, were identified in drone imagery. The I-ORS plume was sustained throughout the tidal cycle, and its orientation varied with tidal phase. Near-bottom sediment dynamics was characterized using an optical backscatter sensor deployed at a depth of 35 m. During the observation period, mean turbidity was 29.7 FTU, reaching 76.2 FTU during the flood phase. These results indicate that sediment resuspension occurs near the seabed and suggest a possible link between near-bottom resuspension and the surface plumes. The integration of satellite imagery, drone observations, and in-situ measurements provides a framework for investigating sediment plume dynamics across multiple spatial scales. Future high-resolution acoustic observations of seabed morphology and local scour around I-ORS will provide further insight into the relationship between near-bottom sediment resuspension and surface plume development.

abstracts.title: Strong and rapid authigenic uptake of potassium: Evidence from the Changjiang (Yangtze) Estuary-East China Sea
affiliations: State Key Laboratory of Marine Geology, Tongji University, Shanghai, China
GEOMAR Helmholtz Centre for Ocean Research Kiel, Kiel, Germany
Universität Hamburg, Hamburg, Germany
